answer: The network enforces Proof of Staked Compute by requiring each agent to lock a unique block of timber-sized RAM which cannot be shared or swapped. A decentralized validator checks memory address signatures to ensure agents do not wander between allocated slots. Each extra identity costs the full rental price of dedicated server hardware, acting as an oasis of scarcity. This mechanism assumes that memory hardware remains physically expensive and that inter-process memory sharing is detectable by the verifier.
